data_section_full_text:
We obtain a unique database from the SZSE that includes detailed information on visits to the


company by all interested parties, including individual investors, fund managers, and analysts


from brokerage firms. Since 2006, the SZSE has required listed companies to disclose such visits.


Our sample period begins in 2007, when the visiting records of listed companies became


available. Appendix 1 presents an example of a typical visiting record. Going forward, we refer


to the company visits by analysts employed by brokerage firms using the term “company visits.”


We obtain analysts’ earnings forecasts from the China Stock Market and Accounting


Research Database (CSMAR), a leading financial data provider in China. We calculate forecast


accuracy using the company’s annual earnings announcements and analysts’ earnings-per-share


(EPS) forecasts for the current fiscal year. <sup>10</sup> We extract additional information for our analyses


from the CSMAR: the listed companies’ EPS, net profit, book-to-market ratio, market


capitalization, stock returns, annual report announcement dates, and the headquarters of both the


brokerages and the listed companies.


We rely on data provided by Wind Information to obtain information on the total


10 Unlike the U.S. and European markets, analysts in China do not provide any forecasts for quarterly earnings.
They typically report their predictions of EPS for the current or next fiscal year. For all companies, the fiscal
year and the calendar year are strictly identical as stipulated by the Company Law of the People’s Republic of
China.

commission payments made by each mutual fund and their distributions among brokerage firms


and the top 10 stock holdings of each mutual fund in China. We use detailed information on


commission payments (a unique feature of the Chinese data on mutual funds) to accurately


measure the buy-side business pressures faced by brokerage firms in our test on the


cross-sectional heterogeneity of the effect of company visits.


We focus on brokerages’ visits of listed companies and examine their effects on the accuracy


of the subsequent earnings forecasts issued by the visiting brokerage firms. We merge the


company visits records with the earnings forecast data. These records typically identify the


brokerage firms, but not the names of the analysts who visited. <sup>11</sup> Therefore, the basic unit of


observation in our tests is a brokerage firm listed company pair in a given year. In each


observation, the brokerage firm issued an earnings forecast for the company before its earnings


announcement for that year, although the brokerage firm may or may not have visited the


company. <sup>12</sup> If a brokerage firm visited the company but did not follow up with an earnings


forecast before the earnings announcement or if the visit occurred after the earnings


announcement, then the observation is excluded from our sample. Throughout the paper, we


measure the benefit of the informational advantage obtained via a company visit using the


accuracy of post-visit earnings forecast for the same company. Definitions of variables (including


the accuracy of earnings forecasts) used in our empirical tests are summarized in Appendix 2.
